standard.title: Systems and software engineering-Systems and software Quality Requirements and Evaluation (SQuaRE)-Product quality model
standard.prepared_by: ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 7, Software and systems engineering
standard.scope: Defines a product quality model applicable to ICT products and software products. The model is, in the words of clause 1, "composed of nine characteristics (which are further subdivided into subcharacteristics)" that relate to quality properties of the product. It is a reference model for specifying, measuring and evaluating product quality, usable across the lifecycle by developers, acquirers, quality assurance staff and independent evaluators. A product here includes software, data, hardware, firmware and communication infrastructure.
standard.cancels_and_replaces: The second edition of ISO/IEC 25010, together with the first edition of ISO/IEC 25002 and the first edition of ISO/IEC 25019, cancels and replaces ISO/IEC 25010:2011, which has been technically revised. Confirmed from the foreword of the standard itself.
changes_from_2011: Safety was added as a quality characteristic, with the subcharacteristics operational constraint, risk identification, fail safe, hazard warning and safe integration.
Usability and portability were replaced with interaction capability and flexibility respectively.
Inclusivity and self-descriptiveness, resistance, and scalability were added as subcharacteristics of interaction capability, security, and flexibility respectively.
User interface aesthetics and maturity were replaced with user engagement and faultlessness respectively.
Accessibility was split into inclusivity and user assistance.
The target of the product quality model was extended to include various types of ICT product and information system.
Several characteristics and subcharacteristics were given more accurate names and definitions.

quality_in_use_moved.statement: The foreword of ISO/IEC 25010:2023 states that the parts of ISO/IEC 25010:2011 other than the product quality model are moved to ISO/IEC 25002 on quality models overview and usage, and to ISO/IEC 25019 on quality-in-use model. Note 1 to entry under clause 3.4 restates it: usability is now defined in the quality-in-use model, ISO/IEC 25019, and interaction capability is a prerequisite for usability.
quality_in_use_moved.overview_standard: ISO/IEC 25002:2024, Quality model overview and usage
quality_in_use_moved.evidence: Foreword and clause 3.4 Note 1 of the ISO/IEC 25010:2023 preview PDF, which is primary text.

standard.usability_is_not_interaction_capability: Clause 3.4 Note 1 draws the line explicitly. Interaction capability is a set of product attributes that enable users to complete tasks. Usability, in ISO/IEC 25019, is an outcome of use judged by effectiveness, efficiency and satisfaction in a context of use. Note 2 adds that interaction capability is a prerequisite for usability. The two are therefore not synonyms and do not live in the same standard.

japanese_edition.replaces: JIS X 25010:2013, which corresponded to ISO/IEC 25010:2011
japanese_edition.note: This is why established Japanese renderings exist for the 2023 names at all. Several Japanese-language articles written before this edition state that the 2023 model had no official Japanese rendering, and that was true when they were written.

japanese_evidence_tiers.tier_a: Read directly from the JIS X 25010:2025 preview PDF published by the Japanese Standards Association. This covers every name the 2023 edition changed or added, because the JIS foreword enumerates them.
japanese_evidence_tiers.tier_b: Not present in the JIS X 25010:2025 preview, because the preview stops before clause 3. These renderings are carried over unchanged from JIS X 25010:2013 and are corroborated by a Japanese article written against the 2023 model. Each such entry carries a ja_note saying so.

Characteristic and subcharacteristic names and definitions for reliability, security, maintainability, flexibility and safety, which are past the end of the ISO preview PDF. Both pages of the paginated list were read.

source_limitations: The body text of JIS X 25010:2025, clause 3, was not read. The JSA preview stops after the foreword, so the tier B Japanese renderings in this file are the JIS X 25010:2013 wording corroborated against a Japanese article written for the 2023 model, and it is possible that the 2025 edition adjusted some of them, since its own foreword says several characteristics and subcharacteristics were given more accurate names.

The ISO/IEC 25010:2023 definitions for reliability, security, maintainability, flexibility and safety were taken from iso25000.com, not from the standard's own clause 3, because the official preview PDF ends at clause 3.4.4. The names are corroborated by the standard's own foreword; the definition wording is not.
